practiceQuestions.q: सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता में मुहरों और 'पुरोहित-राजा' की आवक्ष मूर्ति (bust) को तराशने के लिए मुख्य रूप से किस सामग्री का उपयोग किया गया था?
practiceQuestions.sol: स्टीअटाइट (साबुन का पत्थर) मुहरों और पुरोहित-राजा की मूर्ति बनाने के लिए प्राथमिक सामग्री थी क्योंकि यह कच्ची अवस्था में बहुत नरम होती है और गर्म करने पर कठोर हो जाती है।

practiceQuestions.q: मोहनजो-दड़ो की कांस्य 'नर्तकी' (Dancing Girl) निम्नलिखित में से किस मुद्रा में खड़ी है?
practiceQuestions.sol: नर्तकी की मूर्ति त्रिभंग मुद्रा (तीन झुकाव) में खड़ी है, जिसमें गर्दन, कमर और घुटनों पर झुकाव होता है।

practiceQuestions.q: असाधारण शारीरिक यथार्थवाद प्रदर्शित करने वाला 'लाल बलुआ पत्थर का पुरुष धड़' किस हड़प्पा स्थल से प्राप्त हुआ था?
practiceQuestions.sol: लाल बलुआ पत्थर का पुरुष धड़ हड़प्पा स्थल से प्राप्त हुआ था।

practiceQuestions.q: हड़प्पा के धातु शिल्पकारों द्वारा कांस्य मूर्तियों को ढालने के लिए किस तकनीक का उपयोग किया गया था?
practiceQuestions.sol: सभी प्रमुख हड़प्पा कांस्य मूर्तियों के लिए लुप्त-मोम ढलाई तकनीक (सीर परड्यू) का उपयोग किया गया था।

practiceQuestions.q: हड़प्पा की टेराकोटा मूर्तियों के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
opts: वे मेसोपोटामिया से आयातित दोहरे सांचों का उपयोग करके बनाई गई थीं।
वे पत्थर की मूर्तियों की तुलना में अत्यधिक यथार्थवादी और शारीरिक रूप से परिष्कृत हैं।
वे मुख्य रूप से चिकोटी काटने (pinching) और चिपकाने (applique) की विधि से हाथ से बनाई गई थीं।
वे केवल आयातित सफेद काओलिन मिट्टी से बनाई गई थीं।
practiceQuestions.sol: हड़प्पा टेराकोटा मूर्तियां चिकोटी काटने और चिपकाने की तकनीक का उपयोग करके हाथ से बनाई गई थीं।

practiceQuestions.q: The famous Daimabad hoard of bronze sculptures belongs to which phase of the Indus Valley Civilization?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Daimabad bronze hoard belongs to the Late Harappan phase, showing the survival and spread of metallurgy to the Deccan.

practiceQuestions.q: The bust of the Priest-King shows a shawl draped over which shoulder?
practiceQuestions.sol: The shawl is draped over the left shoulder, leaving the right shoulder and arm bare.

practiceQuestions.q: Which animal is NOT represented in the Daimabad bronze hoard?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Daimabad hoard features a chariot with bulls, an elephant, a rhinoceros, and a water buffalo. Tiger is not present.

practiceQuestions.q: The eyes of the Priest-King bust from Mohenjo-daro are characterized by which of the following?
opts: Wide open and circular, staring straight ahead
Half-closed and elongated, suggesting a meditative state
Completely hollow sockets without any inlay
Carved with detailed eyelashes and pupils
practiceQuestions.sol: The eyes are half-closed and elongated, indicating a dhyana (meditative) posture.

practiceQuestions.q: A realistic bronze figure of a bull has been discovered at which of the following sites?
practiceQuestions.sol: A highly realistic bronze bull figure was recovered from Kalibangan.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Grey Limestone Dancer from Harappa:
1. It depicts a female dancer in a tribhanga pose.
2. It contains socket holes for attaching separate head and limbs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Dancer is a male figure (often associated with proto-Shiva or Nataraja). Statement 2 is correct; it has socket holes.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following metals were alloyed by Harappans to produce bronze?
practiceQuestions.sol: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin (sometimes containing small amounts of arsenic).

practiceQuestions.q: The terracotta Mother Goddess figurines feature cup-like projections on their headdress. What was the likely purpose of these cups?
opts: To store grain offerings during temple rituals
To hold oil or incense for burning, as evidenced by soot stains
To serve as handles for carrying the figurine
practiceQuestions.sol: Soot stains in the cup-like projections suggest they were used to burn incense or oil during worship.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about the 'Dancing Girl' sculpture is FALSE?
opts: She stands in a tribhanga pose.
She is wearing a necklace of cowry-like shells.
Her right arm is completely covered with bangles.
Her hair is tied in a bun resting on her right shoulder.
practiceQuestions.sol: It is her left arm that is covered with 24-25 bangles. Her right arm has only a couple of armlets.

practiceQuestions.q: The unique socket holes in the Red Sandstone Male Torso suggest which sculptural technique?
opts: Multi-piece assembly of separate body parts
practiceQuestions.sol: The socket holes were used to join a separately carved head and limbs to the main torso.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sites has yielded a notable bronze dog and a bronze bird?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal has yielded copper/bronze models of a dog and a bird.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Indus Valley, terracotta toy carts were typically modeled to resemble carts pulled by which animal?
practiceQuestions.sol: The toy carts were designed to be pulled by humped bulls or oxen, which were the primary draft animals of the civilization.

practiceQuestions.q: The Priest-King's beard is carved with neat vertical lines, but his upper lip is shaven. This style indicates which of the following?
opts: Lack of tools to shave the chin
Specific social, religious, or grooming standards of the ruling elite
Accidental chipping of the stone during excavation
practiceQuestions.sol: The shaven upper lip and well-groomed beard indicate specific aesthetic, social, or priestly grooming standards.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was the major source of copper for the Harappan sculptors?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Khetri copper belt in Rajasthan was the primary source of copper for the Indus Valley Civilization.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements is true regarding the availability of tin for Harappan bronze making?
opts: Tin was abundantly available in the Indus plains.
Tin was imported from Afghanistan and Khorasan.
Tin was not used; they only cast pure copper.
Tin mines were located in Southern India near Chennai.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tin is very scarce in the Indian subcontinent. Harappans imported it from Afghanistan, Central Asia (Khorasan), or northeastern India.

practiceQuestions.q: Which animal representation is extremely rare or absent in Harappan terracotta and bronze art?
practiceQuestions.sol: The horse is extremely rare or virtually absent in mainstream Harappan art, reflecting its minor or non-existent role in Mature Harappan culture.

practiceQuestions.q: The trefoil pattern on the Priest-King's shawl is historically associated with which of the following?
opts: A script character from the Indus script
practiceQuestions.sol: The trefoil motif is believed to carry astral or solar significance, and is also found in contemporary Mesopotamian and Egyptian royal contexts.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the 'applique' technique used in Harappan terracottas?
opts: Pressing clay into a pre-carved wooden mold
Attaching separately shaped pieces of clay (like eyes, nose, or necklaces) onto a main figure
Polishing the fired clay with a smooth stone
Chipping away dried clay using copper needles
practiceQuestions.sol: Applique is the technique of adding separate clay pieces (discs, strips) onto the main body of a figurine to represent eyes, ornaments, etc.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site has yielded a terracotta figurine of a ship, indicating seafaring activity?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal, the port city, has yielded terracotta models of boats/ships.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Harappans used iron molds for lost-wax casting.
2. Lost-wax casting was used to make hollow bronze figures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Harappans did not have iron. Clay molds were used. Statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q: The Priest-King wears an ornament on his right arm. What is it?
opts: An armlet with a circular clasp
practiceQuestions.sol: The Priest-King wears a simple armlet with a circular ornament on his right upper arm.

practiceQuestions.q: Which statement best describes the artistic style of Harappan animal terracottas?
opts: They are highly stylized and abstract, with no recognizable animals.
They show a high degree of naturalism and observation, especially in humped bulls.
They were always glazed and painted with blue glaze.
They are identical to Sumerian animal figures.
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappan animal terracottas, especially the humped bull, show realistic observation of muscle folds and dewlaps.

practiceQuestions.q: The headband worn by the Priest-King is called a:
practiceQuestions.sol: The woven headband or ribbon tied around the forehead is referred to as a fillet.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following Indus Valley sites is located in Maharashtra and yielded a hoard of late Harappan bronzes?
practiceQuestions.sol: Daimabad is situated in Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra, on the banks of the Pravara River.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a common feature of Harappan terracotta Mother Goddesses?
opts: They are seated on high thrones.
They wear elaborate heavy necklaces and a gridled loincloth.
They hold infants in both arms.
Their faces are covered in veils.
practiceQuestions.sol: Mother Goddesses wear multiple beaded necklaces, collars, and a short loincloth secured by a broad, clasp-fitted girdle.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the height of the bronze 'Dancing Girl' of Mohenjo-daro?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Dancing Girl is a tiny masterpiece, measuring approximately 10.5 cm (about 4 inches) in height.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the technology of Harappan sculptures, what does 'pinching' mean?
opts: Using copper pliers to shape hot metal
Squeezing clay between fingers to shape features like noses or ears
Engraving lines on stone using a sharp drill
Applying slip onto pottery before firing
practiceQuestions.sol: Pinching refers to manually squeezing wet clay between the thumb and fingers to shape features directly from the clay mass.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sculptures displays a flat, rectangular face with a shaven upper lip?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Priest-King bust features a shaven upper lip, flat nose, and a well-groomed beard.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about the 'Male Dancer' from Harappa is correct?
opts: It is made of bronze using lost-wax casting.
It is carved from grey limestone and shows a dynamic twisted pose.
It represents a female figure holding a mirror.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Male Dancer is made of grey limestone, has socket joints, and stands in a dynamic twisting pose.

practiceQuestions.q: The bronze figurines of Daimabad were found on wheeled platforms. What does this suggest?
opts: They were meant to be rolled as child toys.
They were designed for easy transport during nomadic movements.
They had mobile ceremonial or ritual uses.
They were imported from Greek toy makers.
practiceQuestions.sol: Wheeled platforms suggest they had ceremonial significance and were dragged during rituals.

practiceQuestions.q: What pigment was originally used to fill the trefoil patterns on the Priest-King's shawl?
practiceQuestions.sol: Archaeological analysis indicates the trefoils were originally filled with a red pigment or paste.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sites has yielded terracotta masks with horned deities?
practiceQuestions.sol: Terracotta horned masks and figurines have been excavated from Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.

practiceQuestions.q: The metallurgy of the Harappan civilization was characterized by which of the following?
opts: Gold leaf gilding on iron frames
Complete absence of lead or tin alloys
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappan metallurgy used copper-tin and copper-arsenic alloys to cast bronze tools and sculptures.

practiceQuestions.q:
Which of the following statements regarding the 'Dancing Girl' sculpture is correct?
1. She represents a formal court dancer waiting for performance.
2. Her posture shows a relaxed, casual attitude with her hand on her hip.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: She stands in a relaxed, almost insolent posture with her hand on her hip, rather than a formal, stiff courtly pose.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary significance of the Red Sandstone Torso's musculature?
opts: It represents a skinny, starving individual.
It represents a plump, breath-filled (prana) abdomen, foreshadowing later Indian yogic sculpture.
It displays exact copies of Greek classical anatomy.
It has no muscle details, being a simple block.
practiceQuestions.sol: The soft, slightly protruding abdomen indicates a prana (life-breath) quality, which became a foundational element of later Indian art.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following features is shared by BOTH the Red Sandstone Torso and the Grey Limestone Dancer?
opts: Both have socket holes for detachable head and limbs.
practiceQuestions.sol: Both Harappa stone sculptures feature socket holes for attaching separate heads and limbs.

practiceQuestions.q: The use of soft stone like steatite for carving reflects which aspect of Harappan craft organization?
opts: Lack of access to harder stones like granite
Systematic exploitation of local talc resources and specialized micro-tools
Import of raw soapstone blocks from Egypt
A religious prohibition against carving hard rocks
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappans systematically quarried steatite from Rajasthan and Gujarat and used specialized copper-alloy drills/chisels to shape them.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following terracotta toys represents a mechanical bird?
opts: A bird that can flap its wings when a string is pulled
A bird with wheels for feet
A bird that dips its beak into water
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappans manufactured bird-shaped whistles that produce sound when blown.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statement is correct about Harappan bronze casting?
opts: It was restricted to small personal amulets.
It was used to manufacture large structural pillars.
It was used for producing both utility items (utensils, axes) and art pieces.
It was completely abandoned in the Mature Harappan phase.
practiceQuestions.sol: Bronze metallurgy was used for making tools, mirrors, knives, utensils, and artistic sculptures.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Priest-King' bust was discovered by which archaeologist?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Priest-King was discovered during the excavations led by Sir John Marshall's team at Mohenjo-daro.

practiceQuestions.q: The armlet worn by the Priest-King contains which decorative feature?
opts: A small figure of a bull
practiceQuestions.sol: The armlet has a circular clasp, matching the clasp on his headband.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about Harappan terracottas is FALSE?
opts: Terracottas were made of fire-baked clay.
They are found in both elite public zones and common residential houses.
They are far more numerous than stone and bronze sculptures combined.
They were used exclusively as currency coins.
practiceQuestions.sol: They were toys, decorative items, or religious figures, NOT currency coins.

practiceQuestions.q: The Daimabad bronze elephant and rhinoceros are mounted on wheeled platforms. What does this indicate?
opts: They had mobile ceremonial or religious functions.
They were replicas of war machines.
They were exported to Roman festivals.
practiceQuestions.sol: The wheeled platforms suggest they were dragged in ceremonial or ritual processions.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'prana' (breath) concept in the Red Sandstone Torso refers to which aesthetic quality?
opts: A soft, rounded abdominal profile suggesting the body is filled with life-breath
Engraved wind symbols on the back
Hollow channels inside the chest to allow air to pass through
practiceQuestions.sol: Prana refers to the yogic concept of life-breath, represented in art as a soft, full, rounded abdomen rather than tight muscles.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the hair of the bronze Dancing Girl?
opts: Cropped short like a modern bob cut
Tied in a heavy bun resting on her right shoulder
Left loose and flowing down to her waist
practiceQuestions.sol: The Dancing Girl's hair is tied in a neat, heavy bun that rests on her right shoulder.
